paper.title: SNooPy: a statistical framework for long-read metagenomic variant calling
paper.authors: Faure R, Faure U, Truong T, Derzelle A, Lavenier D, Flot J, Quince C.

steps.evidence: The algorithm begins by transforming read alignments from BAM format into binary matrices suitable for variant calling.
we partition the reference genome into fixed-length windows and only consider reads that span the full window.
We set the window length to half the median read length
To exploit this signal, we cluster reads within each window based on their mapping coordinates. Groups of at least 5 reads sharing exactly the same mapping coordinates are grouped together
To enhance computational efficiency and statistical power, we only include loci where alternative alleles appear in more than 5% of reads.
To identify candidate variants, the algorithm starts by computing pairwise correlations between all columns using chi-square tests, yielding a p-value for each pair of columns.
This p-value is used to perform complete-linkage hierarchical clustering with a p-value cutoff of 0.05 to group highly correlated columns.
We reject the null hypothesis when p ≤ 0.001.
When a pattern passes the test, the corresponding variants are outputted in a VCF file.

For each genomic position, we model the expected number of sequencing errors as following a binomial distribution with parameters c (the coverage at that position) and s (the maximum error rate). When an alternative allele appears at a frequency that yields a p-value smaller than 0.001 under this null model, we classify the position as an “obvious” SNP

After establishing high-confidence variant calls, we perform a recovery phase where all loci are tested for correlation with confirmed SNPs using chi-square tests. Positions demonstrating significant correlation (p-value < 10−6) with established variants are rescued and called as SNPs.

To address this limitation, we perform iterative variant calling. After the initial round, all called variants are masked (i.e., converted to reference-like status in the binary matrix), and the algorithm is re-executed on the modified data.
